   751→fn capitalize(s: &str) -> String {
   752→    let mut chars = s.chars();
   753→    match chars.next() {
   754→        None => String::new(),
   755→        Some(c) => c.to_uppercase().to_string() + chars.as_str(),
   756→    }
   757→}
   758→
   759→fn is_owner_user(jid: &Jid, own_pn: Option<&Jid>, own_lid: Option<&Jid>) -> bool {
   760→    own_pn.is_some_and(|pn| pn.is_same_user_as(jid))
   761→        || own_lid.is_some_and(|lid| lid.is_same_user_as(jid))
   762→}
   763→
   764→fn context_info_mentions_owner(
   765→    context: Option<&wa::ContextInfo>,
   766→    own_pn: Option<&Jid>,
   767→    own_lid: Option<&Jid>,
   768→) -> bool {
   769→    context.is_some_and(|context| {
   770→        context.mentioned_jid.iter().any(|mentioned| {
   771→            mentioned
   772→                .parse::<Jid>()
   773→                .ok()
   774→                .is_some_and(|jid| is_owner_user(&jid, own_pn, own_lid))
   775→        })
   776→    })
   777→}
   778→
   779→fn message_mentions_owner(msg: &wa::Message, own_pn: Option<&Jid>, own_lid: Option<&Jid>) -> bool {
   780→    context_info_mentions_owner(
   781→        msg.extended_text_message
   782→            .as_ref()
   783→            .and_then(|message| message.context_info.as_deref()),
   784→        own_pn,
   785→        own_lid,
   786→    ) || context_info_mentions_owner(
   787→        msg.image_message
   788→            .as_ref()
   789→            .and_then(|message| message.context_info.as_deref()),
   790→        own_pn,
   791→        own_lid,
   792→    ) || context_info_mentions_owner(
   793→        msg.audio_message
   794→            .as_ref()
   795→            .and_then(|message| message.context_info.as_deref()),
   796→        own_pn,
   797→        own_lid,
   798→    ) || context_info_mentions_owner(
   799→        msg.video_message
   800→            .as_ref()
   801→            .and_then(|message| message.context_info.as_deref()),
   802→        own_pn,
   803→        own_lid,
   804→    ) || context_info_mentions_owner(
   805→        msg.document_message
   806→            .as_ref()
   807→            .and_then(|message| message.context_info.as_deref()),
   808→        own_pn,
   809→        own_lid,
   810→    )
   811→}
   812→
   813→fn should_ignore_inbound_chat(source: &wacore::types::message::MessageSource) -> bool {
   814→    source.chat.is_status_broadcast() || source.is_incoming_broadcast()
   815→}
   816→
   817→fn is_benign_self_chat_protocol_message(msg: &wa::Message) -> bool {
   818→    msg.sender_key_distribution_message.is_some()
   819→        || msg.protocol_message.is_some()
   820→        || msg.reaction_message.is_some()
   821→        || msg.edited_message.is_some()
   822→        || msg.event_message.is_some()
   823→}
   824→
   825→/// List which `Option` fields on `wa::Message` are `Some`, giving operators a
   826→/// concrete clue about the unhandled message type (e.g. "sticker_message, reaction_message").
   827→///
   828→/// Only checks fields that are NOT already handled by `classify_message` to avoid
   829→/// misleading output — if a field appears here it genuinely was not dispatched.
   830→fn describe_message_fields(msg: &wa::Message) -> String {
   831→    let mut present = Vec::new();
   832→    macro_rules! check {
   833→        ($($field:ident),+ $(,)?) => {
   834→            $(if msg.$field.is_some() { present.push(stringify!($field)); })+
   835→        };
   836→    }
   837→    // Omit fields already handled by classify_message:
   838→    //   conversation, extended_text_message, image_message, audio_message,
   839→    //   video_message, document_message, location_message, live_location_message
   840→    check!(
   841→        sender_key_distribution_message,
   842→        contact_message,
   843→        call,
   844→        protocol_message,
   845→        contacts_array_message,
   846→        sticker_message,
   847→        reaction_message,
   848→        poll_creation_message,
   849→        poll_update_message,
   850→        interactive_message,
   851→        edited_message,
   852→        event_message,
   853→    );
   854→    if present.is_empty() {
   855→        "none".to_owned()
   856→    } else {
   857→        present.join(", ")
   858→    }
   859→}
   860→
   861→/// Classify the inbound message kind based on its content.
   862→///
   863→/// Media types take priority over text — an image with a caption is still `Photo`,
   864→/// not `Text`. This ensures the media handler runs and can include the caption
   865→/// alongside the attachment.
   866→fn classify_message(msg: &wa::Message, text: &str) -> ChannelMessageKind {
   867→    if msg.image_message.is_some() {
   868→        ChannelMessageKind::Photo
   869→    } else if msg.audio_message.is_some() {
   870→        if msg
   871→            .audio_message
   872→            .as_ref()
   873→            .is_some_and(|a| a.ptt.unwrap_or(false))
   874→        {
   875→            ChannelMessageKind::Voice
   876→        } else {
   877→            ChannelMessageKind::Audio
   878→        }
   879→    } else if msg.video_message.is_some() {
   880→        ChannelMessageKind::Video
   881→    } else if msg.document_message.is_some() {
   882→        ChannelMessageKind::Document
   883→    } else if msg.location_message.is_some() || msg.live_location_message.is_some() {
   884→        ChannelMessageKind::Location
   885→    } else if !text.is_empty() {
   886→        ChannelMessageKind::Text
   887→    } else {
   888→        ChannelMessageKind::Other
   889→    }
   890→}
   891→
   892→/// Handle OTP challenge/verification flow for a non-allowlisted DM user.
   893→///
   894→/// Called when `dm_policy = Allowlist`, the peer is not on the allowlist, and
   895→/// `otp_self_approval` is enabled.
   896→#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
   897→async fn handle_otp_flow(
   898→    accounts: &AccountStateMap,
   899→    account_id: &str,
   900→    peer_id: &str,
   901→    username: Option<&str>,
   902→    sender_name: Option<&str>,
   903→    body: &str,
   904→    chat_jid: &Jid,
   905→    state: &AccountState,
   906→) {
   907→    let has_pending = {
   908→        let accts = accounts.read().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
   909→        accts
   910→            .get(account_id)
   911→            .map(|s| {
   912→                let otp = s.otp.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
   913→                otp.has_pending(peer_id)
   914→            })
   915→            .unwrap_or(false)
   916→    };
   917→
   918→    if has_pending {
   919→        let trimmed = body.trim();
   920→        if trimmed.len() != 6 || !trimmed.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
   921→            // Non-code message while OTP pending — silently ignore.
   922→            return;
   923→        }
   924→
   925→        let result = {
   926→            let accts = accounts.read().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
   927→            match accts.get(account_id) {
   928→                Some(s) => {
   929→                    let mut otp = s.otp.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
   930→                    otp.verify(peer_id, trimmed)
   931→                },
   932→                None => return,
   933→            }
   934→        };
   935→
   936→        match result {
   937→            OtpVerifyResult::Approved => {
   938→                approve_sender_via_otp(
   939→                    state.event_sink.as_deref(),
   940→                    ChannelType::Whatsapp,
   941→                    account_id,
   942→                    peer_id,
   943→                    peer_id,
   944→                    username,
   945→                )
   946→                .await;
   947→
   948→                let reply = wa::Message {
   949→                    conversation: Some("Access granted! You can now use this bot.".into()),
   950→                    ..Default::default()
   951→                };
   952→                let _ = state.send_message(chat_jid.clone(), reply).await;
   953→            },
   954→            OtpVerifyResult::WrongCode { attempts_left } => {
   955→                let reply = wa::Message {
   956→                    conversation: Some(format!(
   957→                        "Wrong code. {attempts_left} attempt{} remaining.",
   958→                        if attempts_left == 1 {
   959→                            ""
   960→                        } else {
   961→                            "s"
   962→                        }
   963→                    )),
   964→                    ..Default::default()
   965→                };
   966→                let _ = state.send_message(chat_jid.clone(), reply).await;
   967→            },
   968→            OtpVerifyResult::LockedOut => {
   969→                let reply = wa::Message {
   970→                    conversation: Some("Too many failed attempts. Please try again later.".into()),
   971→                    ..Default::default()
   972→                };
   973→                let _ = state.send_message(chat_jid.clone(), reply).await;
   974→                emit_otp_resolution(
   975→                    state.event_sink.as_deref(),
   976→                    ChannelType::Whatsapp,
   977→                    account_id,
   978→                    peer_id,
   979→                    username,
   980→                    "locked_out",
   981→                )
   982→                .await;
   983→            },
   984→            OtpVerifyResult::Expired => {
   985→                let reply = wa::Message {
   986→                    conversation: Some(
   987→                        "Your code has expired. Please send any message to get a new code.".into(),
   988→                    ),
   989→                    ..Default::default()
   990→                };
   991→                let _ = state.send_message(chat_jid.clone(), reply).await;
   992→                emit_otp_resolution(
   993→                    state.event_sink.as_deref(),
   994→                    ChannelType::Whatsapp,
   995→                    account_id,
   996→                    peer_id,
   997→                    username,
   998→                    "expired",
   999→                )
  1000→                .await;
  1001→            },
  1002→            OtpVerifyResult::NoPending => {},
  1003→        }
  1004→        return;
  1005→    }
  1006→
  1007→    // No pending challenge — initiate one.
  1008→    let init_result = {
  1009→        let accts = accounts.read().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
  1010→        match accts.get(account_id) {
  1011→            Some(s) => {
  1012→                let mut otp = s.otp.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
  1013→                otp.initiate(
  1014→                    peer_id,
  1015→                    username.map(String::from),
  1016→                    sender_name.map(String::from),
  1017→                )
  1018→            },
  1019→            None => return,
  1020→        }
  1021→    };
  1022→
  1023→    match init_result {
  1024→        OtpInitResult::Created(code) => {
  1025→            info!(account_id, peer_id, code, "OTP challenge issued");
  1026→            let reply = wa::Message {
  1027→                conversation: Some(OTP_CHALLENGE_MSG.to_string()),
  1028→                ..Default::default()
  1029→            };
  1030→            let _ = state.send_message(chat_jid.clone(), reply).await;
  1031→
  1032→            // Compute expires_at as epoch seconds (5 minutes from now).
  1033→            let expires_at = std::time::SystemTime::now()
  1034→                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
  1035→                .unwrap_or_default()
  1036→                .as_secs() as i64
  1037→                + 300;
  1038→
  1039→            emit_otp_challenge(
  1040→                state.event_sink.as_deref(),
  1041→                ChannelType::Whatsapp,
  1042→                account_id,
  1043→                peer_id,
  1044→                username,
  1045→                sender_name,
  1046→                code,
  1047→                expires_at,
  1048→            )
  1049→            .await;
  1050→        },
  1051→        OtpInitResult::AlreadyPending => {
  1052→            // Resend the challenge message.
  1053→            let reply = wa::Message {
  1054→                conversation: Some(OTP_CHALLENGE_MSG.to_string()),
  1055→                ..Default::default()
  1056→            };
  1057→            let _ = state.send_message(chat_jid.clone(), reply).await;
  1058→        },
  1059→        OtpInitResult::LockedOut => {
  1060→            let reply = wa::Message {
  1061→                conversation: Some("Too many failed attempts. Please try again later.".into()),
  1062→                ..Default::default()
  1063→            };
  1064→            let _ = state.send_message(chat_jid.clone(), reply).await;
  1065→        },
  1066→    }
  1067→}

//! Storage traits for the WhatsApp client.
//!
//! This module defines 4 domain-grouped traits that together form the `Backend` trait:
//!
//! - [`SignalStore`]: Signal protocol cryptographic operations (identity, sessions, keys)
//! - [`AppSyncStore`]: WhatsApp app state synchronization
//! - [`ProtocolStore`]: WhatsApp Web protocol alignment (SKDM, LID mapping, device registry)
//! - [`DeviceStore`]: Device persistence operations

use crate::appstate::hash::HashState;
use crate::store::error::Result;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use wacore_appstate::processor::AppStateMutationMAC;
use wacore_binary::jid::Jid;

/// App state synchronization key for WhatsApp's app state protocol.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct AppStateSyncKey {
    pub key_data: Vec<u8>,
    pub fingerprint: Vec<u8>,
    pub timestamp: i64,
}

/// Entry representing a LID to Phone Number mapping.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct LidPnMappingEntry {
    /// The LID user part (e.g., "100000012345678")
    pub lid: String,
    /// The phone number user part (e.g., "559980000001")
    pub phone_number: String,
    /// Unix timestamp when the mapping was first learned
    pub created_at: i64,
    /// Unix timestamp when the mapping was last updated
    pub updated_at: i64,
    /// The source from which this mapping was learned (e.g., "usync", "peer_pn_message")
    pub learning_source: String,
}

/// Trusted contact privacy token entry.
///
/// Matches WhatsApp Web's Chat.tcToken / tcTokenTimestamp / tcTokenSenderTimestamp.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TcTokenEntry {
    /// Raw token bytes received from the server.
    pub token: Vec<u8>,
    /// Unix timestamp (seconds) when the token was received.
    pub token_timestamp: i64,
    /// Unix timestamp (seconds) when we last issued our token to this contact.
    pub sender_timestamp: Option<i64>,
}

/// Device information for registry tracking.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DeviceInfo {
    /// The device ID (0 = primary device, 1+ = companion devices)
    pub device_id: u32,
    /// The key index, if known
    pub key_index: Option<u32>,
}

/// Device list record matching WhatsApp Web's DeviceListRecord structure.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DeviceListRecord {
    /// The user part of the JID (phone number or LID)
    pub user: String,
    /// List of known devices for this user
    pub devices: Vec<DeviceInfo>,
    /// Timestamp when this record was last updated
    pub timestamp: i64,
    /// Participant hash from usync, if available
    pub phash: Option<String>,
}

/// Signal protocol cryptographic storage operations.
///
/// Handles identity keys, sessions, pre-keys, signed pre-keys, and sender keys
/// for end-to-end encryption.
#[cfg_attr(target_arch = "wasm32", async_trait(?Send))]
#[cfg_attr(not(target_arch = "wasm32"), async_trait)]
pub trait SignalStore: Send + Sync {
    // --- Identity Operations ---

    /// Store an identity key for a remote address.
    async fn put_identity(&self, address: &str, key: [u8; 32]) -> Result<()>;

    /// Load an identity key for a remote address.
    async fn load_identity(&self, address: &str) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>;

    /// Delete an identity key.
    async fn delete_identity(&self, address: &str) -> Result<()>;

    // --- Session Operations ---

    /// Get an encrypted session for an address.
    async fn get_session(&self, address: &str) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>;

    /// Store an encrypted session.
    async fn put_session(&self, address: &str, session: &[u8]) -> Result<()>;

    /// Delete a session.
    async fn delete_session(&self, address: &str) -> Result<()>;

    /// Check if a session exists. Default implementation uses `get_session`.
    async fn has_session(&self, address: &str) -> Result<bool> {
        Ok(self.get_session(address).await?.is_some())
    }

    // --- PreKey Operations ---

    /// Store a pre-key.
    async fn store_prekey(&self, id: u32, record: &[u8], uploaded: bool) -> Result<()>;

    /// Store multiple pre-keys in a single batch operation.
    /// Default implementation falls back to individual `store_prekey` calls.
    async fn store_prekeys_batch(&self, keys: &[(u32, Vec<u8>)], uploaded: bool) -> Result<()> {
        for (id, record) in keys {
            self.store_prekey(*id, record, uploaded).await?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Load a pre-key by ID.
    async fn load_prekey(&self, id: u32) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>;

    /// Remove a pre-key.
    async fn remove_prekey(&self, id: u32) -> Result<()>;

    /// Get the maximum pre-key ID currently stored, or 0 if none exist.
    /// Used for migration when `next_pre_key_id` counter is not yet initialized.
    async fn get_max_prekey_id(&self) -> Result<u32>;

    // --- Signed PreKey Operations ---

    /// Store a signed pre-key.
    async fn store_signed_prekey(&self, id: u32, record: &[u8]) -> Result<()>;

    /// Load a signed pre-key by ID.
    async fn load_signed_prekey(&self, id: u32) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>;

    /// Load all signed pre-keys. Returns (id, record) pairs.
    async fn load_all_signed_prekeys(&self) -> Result<Vec<(u32, Vec<u8>)>>;

    /// Remove a signed pre-key.
    async fn remove_signed_prekey(&self, id: u32) -> Result<()>;

    // --- Sender Key Operations ---

    /// Store a sender key for group messaging.
    async fn put_sender_key(&self, address: &str, record: &[u8]) -> Result<()>;

    /// Get a sender key.
    async fn get_sender_key(&self, address: &str) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>;

    /// Delete a sender key.
    async fn delete_sender_key(&self, address: &str) -> Result<()>;
}

/// WhatsApp app state synchronization storage.
///
/// Handles sync keys, version tracking, and mutation MACs for the app state protocol.
#[cfg_attr(target_arch = "wasm32", async_trait(?Send))]
#[cfg_attr(not(target_arch = "wasm32"), async_trait)]
pub trait AppSyncStore: Send + Sync {
    /// Get an app state sync key by ID.
    async fn get_sync_key(&self, key_id: &[u8]) -> Result<Option<AppStateSyncKey>>;

    /// Set an app state sync key.
    async fn set_sync_key(&self, key_id: &[u8], key: AppStateSyncKey) -> Result<()>;

    /// Get the app state version for a collection.
    async fn get_version(&self, name: &str) -> Result<HashState>;

    /// Set the app state version for a collection.
    async fn set_version(&self, name: &str, state: HashState) -> Result<()>;

    /// Store mutation MACs for a version.
    async fn put_mutation_macs(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        version: u64,
        mutations: &[AppStateMutationMAC],
    ) -> Result<()>;

    /// Get a mutation MAC by index.
    async fn get_mutation_mac(&self, name: &str, index_mac: &[u8]) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>;

    /// Delete mutation MACs by their index MACs.
    async fn delete_mutation_macs(&self, name: &str, index_macs: &[Vec<u8>]) -> Result<()>;

    /// Get the most recently stored app state sync key ID.
    async fn get_latest_sync_key_id(&self) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>;
}

/// WhatsApp Web protocol alignment storage.
///
/// Handles SKDM tracking, LID-PN mapping, base key collision detection,
/// device registry, and sender key status.
#[cfg_attr(target_arch = "wasm32", async_trait(?Send))]
#[cfg_attr(not(target_arch = "wasm32"), async_trait)]
pub trait ProtocolStore: Send + Sync {
    // --- SKDM Tracking ---

    /// Get device JIDs that have received SKDM for a group.
    async fn get_skdm_recipients(&self, group_jid: &str) -> Result<Vec<Jid>>;

    /// Record devices that have received SKDM for a group.
    async fn add_skdm_recipients(&self, group_jid: &str, device_jids: &[Jid]) -> Result<()>;

    /// Clear SKDM recipients for a group (call when sender key is rotated).
    async fn clear_skdm_recipients(&self, group_jid: &str) -> Result<()>;

    // --- LID-PN Mapping ---

    /// Get a mapping by LID.
    async fn get_lid_mapping(&self, lid: &str) -> Result<Option<LidPnMappingEntry>>;

    /// Get a mapping by phone number (returns the most recent LID for that phone).
    async fn get_pn_mapping(&self, phone: &str) -> Result<Option<LidPnMappingEntry>>;

    /// Store or update a LID-PN mapping.
    async fn put_lid_mapping(&self, entry: &LidPnMappingEntry) -> Result<()>;

    /// Get all LID-PN mappings (for cache warm-up).
    async fn get_all_lid_mappings(&self) -> Result<Vec<LidPnMappingEntry>>;

    // --- Base Key Collision Detection ---

    /// Save the base key for a session address during retry collision detection.
    async fn save_base_key(&self, address: &str, message_id: &str, base_key: &[u8]) -> Result<()>;

    /// Check if the current session has the same base key as the saved one.
    async fn has_same_base_key(
        &self,
        address: &str,
        message_id: &str,
        current_base_key: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<bool>;

    /// Delete a base key entry.
    async fn delete_base_key(&self, address: &str, message_id: &str) -> Result<()>;

    // --- Device Registry ---

    /// Update the device list for a user (called after usync responses).
    async fn update_device_list(&self, record: DeviceListRecord) -> Result<()>;

    /// Get all known devices for a user.
    async fn get_devices(&self, user: &str) -> Result<Option<DeviceListRecord>>;

    // --- Sender Key Status (Lazy Deletion) ---

    /// Mark a participant's sender key as needing regeneration for a group.
    async fn mark_forget_sender_key(&self, group_jid: &str, participant: &str) -> Result<()>;

    /// Get participants that need fresh SKDM (marked for forget).
    /// Consumes the marks (deletes them after reading).
    async fn consume_forget_marks(&self, group_jid: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>>;

    // --- TcToken Storage ---

    /// Get a trusted contact token for a JID (stored under LID).
    async fn get_tc_token(&self, jid: &str) -> Result<Option<TcTokenEntry>>;

    /// Store or update a trusted contact token for a JID.
    async fn put_tc_token(&self, jid: &str, entry: &TcTokenEntry) -> Result<()>;

    /// Delete a trusted contact token for a JID.
    async fn delete_tc_token(&self, jid: &str) -> Result<()>;

    /// Get all JIDs that have stored tc tokens.
    async fn get_all_tc_token_jids(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>>;

    /// Delete tc tokens with token_timestamp older than cutoff. Returns count deleted.
    async fn delete_expired_tc_tokens(&self, cutoff_timestamp: i64) -> Result<u32>;

    // --- Sent Message Store (retry support, matches WA Web's getMessageTable) ---

    /// Store a sent message's serialized payload for retry handling.
    /// Called after each send_message(); the payload is the protobuf-encoded Message.
    async fn store_sent_message(
        &self,
        chat_jid: &str,
        message_id: &str,
        payload: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<()>;

    /// Retrieve and delete a sent message (atomic take). Returns serialized payload.
    /// Called when a retry receipt arrives; consuming prevents double-retry.
    async fn take_sent_message(&self, chat_jid: &str, message_id: &str) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>;

    /// Delete sent messages older than cutoff (unix timestamp seconds). Returns count deleted.
    async fn delete_expired_sent_messages(&self, cutoff_timestamp: i64) -> Result<u32>;
}

/// Device data persistence operations.
#[cfg_attr(target_arch = "wasm32", async_trait(?Send))]
#[cfg_attr(not(target_arch = "wasm32"), async_trait)]
pub trait DeviceStore: Send + Sync {
    /// Save device data.
    async fn save(&self, device: &crate::store::Device) -> Result<()>;

    /// Load device data.
    async fn load(&self) -> Result<Option<crate::store::Device>>;

    /// Check if a device exists.
    async fn exists(&self) -> Result<bool>;

    /// Create a new device row and return its generated device_id.
    async fn create(&self) -> Result<i32>;

    /// Create a snapshot of the database state.
    /// The argument `name` can be used to label the snapshot file.
    /// `extra_content` can be used to save a related binary blob (e.g. the message that caused the failure).
    async fn snapshot_db(&self, _name: &str, _extra_content: Option<&[u8]>) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Combined storage backend trait.
///
/// Any type implementing all four domain traits automatically implements `Backend`.
pub trait Backend: SignalStore + AppSyncStore + ProtocolStore + DeviceStore + Send + Sync {}

impl<T> Backend for T where T: SignalStore + AppSyncStore + ProtocolStore + DeviceStore + Send + Sync
{}

  "old_string": "#[async_trait]\nimpl ProtocolStore for SledStore {\n    async fn get_skdm_recipients(&self, group_jid: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n        match self\n            .skdm_recipients\n            .get(group_jid.as_bytes())\n            .map_err(db_err)?\n        {\n            Some(v) => decode_persistent(&v),\n            None => Ok(Vec::new()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    async fn add_skdm_recipients(&self, group_jid: &str, device_jids: &[String]) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut current = self.get_skdm_recipients(group_jid).await?;\n        current.extend(device_jids.iter().cloned());\n        let val = encode_persistent(&current)?;\n        self.skdm_recipients\n            .insert(group_jid.as_bytes(), val.as_slice())\n            .map_err(db_err)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }",
  "new_string": "#[async_trait]\nimpl ProtocolStore for SledStore {\n    async fn get_skdm_recipients(&self, group_jid: &str) -> Result<Vec<Jid>> {\n        match self\n            .skdm_recipients\n            .get(group_jid.as_bytes())\n            .map_err(db_err)?\n        {\n            // Stored as Vec<String> for serialization, parse back to Jid.\n            Some(v) => {\n                let strings: Vec<String> = decode_persistent(&v)?;\n                Ok(strings\n                    .into_iter()\n                    .filter_map(|s| s.parse().ok())\n                    .collect())\n            },\n            None => Ok(Vec::new()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    async fn add_skdm_recipients(&self, group_jid: &str, device_jids: &[Jid]) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut current: Vec<String> = match self\n            .skdm_recipients\n            .get(group_jid.as_bytes())\n            .map_err(db_err)?\n        {\n            Some(v) => decode_persistent(&v)?,\n            None => Vec::new(),\n        };\n        current.extend(device_jids.iter().map(|j| j.to_string()));\n        let val = encode_persistent(&current)?;\n        self.skdm_recipients\n            .insert(group_jid.as_bytes(), val.as_slice())\n            .map_err(db_err)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }"
}

  .map_err(db_err)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn take_sent_message(\n        &self,\n        chat_jid: &str,\n        message_id: &str,\n    ) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {\n        let key decode_persistent(&v)?;\n                Ok(Some(payload))\n            },\n            None => Ok(None),\n        }\n    }\n\n    async fn delete_expired_sent_messages(&self, cutoff_timestamp: i64) -> Result<u32> {\n        let mut count = 0u32;\n        let mut keys_to_remove = Vec::new();\n        for entry in self.sent_messages.iter() {\n            let (k, v) = entry.map_err(db_err)?;\n            let (_payload, ts): (Vec<u8>, u64) = decode_persistent(&v)?;\n            if (ts as i64) < cutoff_timestamp {\n                keys_to_remove.push(k);\n            }\n        }\n        for key in keys_to_remove {\n            self.sent_messages.remove(key).map_err(db_err)?;\n            count += 1;\n        }\n        Ok(count)\n    }\n}"

e.key().clone())\n            .collect();\n        let count = keys_to_remove.len() as u32;\n        for key in keys_to_remove {\n            self.sent_messages.remove(&key);\n        }\n        Ok(count)\n    }\n}"
}

Perfect! Now I have all the information needed. Let me provide a comprehensive report.

## Summary: Channel Configuration in Onboarding Flow and Settings UI

### 1. **Where the List of Available/Default Channels is Defined**

**Configuration Schema** (`crates/config/src/schema/runtime.rs`, lines 206-295):
- `ChannelsConfig` struct with `offered: Vec<String>` field
- **Default channels** (if not configured):
  ```rust
  vec![
      "telegram".into(),
      "msteams".into(),
      "discord".into(),
      "slack".into(),
      "matrix".into(),
      "nostr".into(),
  ]
  ```
- **Important**: WhatsApp is intentionally NOT in the default list; it must be explicitly added to `[channels].offered` in `moltis.toml`
- Users add it via: `offered = ["telegram", "msteams", "discord", "slack", "matrix", "nostr", "whatsapp"]`

**Config Documentation** (`crates/config/src/template.rs`, lines 852-858):
```toml
[channels]
# Add "whatsapp" to enable it in the UI.
# offered = ["telegram", "msteams", "discord", "slack", "matrix", "nostr", "whatsapp"]
```

### 2. **How Existing Channels are Registered as Available**

**Channel Type Enum** (`crates/channels/src/plugin.rs`, lines 17-26):
Defined as:
```rust
pub enum ChannelType {
    Telegram,
    Whatsapp,
    #[serde(rename = "msteams")]
    MsTeams,
    Discord,
    Slack,
    Matrix,
    Nostr,
}
```

**All 7 Channels are Fully Registered**:
- Each has `descriptor()` method returning `ChannelDescriptor` with capabilities
- Each has `secret_fields()` defining which fields are secrets
- Each has display names and string conversions (e.g., `as_str()`, `display_name()`)
- Slack and Discord are complete in both onboarding and settings pages

### 3. **Onboarding UI Code**

**Main Files**:
- `/crates/web/src/assets/js/onboarding-view.js` - Preact-based onboarding wizard
- `/crates/web/src/assets/js/page-channels.js` - Settings channels page

**Channel Selection** (`onboarding-view.js`, lines 2366-2375):
```javascript
function ChannelTypeSelector({ onSelect, offered }) {
    var channelOptions = [
        ["telegram", "icon-telegram", "Telegram"],
        ["whatsapp", "icon-whatsapp", "WhatsApp"],
        ["msteams", "icon-msteams", "Microsoft Teams"],
        ["discord", "icon-discord", "Discord"],
        ["matrix", "icon-matrix", "Matrix"],
        ["nostr", "icon-nostr", "Nostr"],
    ].filter(([type]) => offered.has(type));
```

**Note**: Slack is NOT in the onboarding channel selector at all - no entry in the channelOptions array. This is intentional.

**Onboarding Forms Implemented**:
- TelegramForm (line 2723)
- WhatsAppForm (line 3325)
- TeamsForm (line 2818)
- DiscordForm (line 3000)
- MatrixForm (line 3107)
- NostrForm (line 3510)
- **NO SlackForm in onboarding** - Slack can only be added from the Settings Channels page

### 4. **Settings/Channels Pages**

**File**: `/crates/web/src/assets/js/page-channels.js`

**Connect Buttons** (lines 444-510):
Shows buttons for all channels IF they're in `channels_offered`:
```javascript
var offered = new Set(getGon("channels_offered") || 
    ["telegram", "discord", "slack", "matrix"]);
```

**Important Difference**: The page-channels default fallback includes "slack" and "discord" (and excludes "msteams", "whatsapp", "nostr").

**All 7 Channels Have Forms**:
- Telegram: lines 620-750
- WhatsApp: lines 751-1100
- Microsoft Teams: lines 1101-1155
- **Slack**: lines 1155-1300
- Discord: lines 1301-1350
- Matrix: lines 1351-2100+
- Nostr: lines 2100+

### 5. **WhatsApp vs Other Channels - Current Referencing**

**WhatsApp Status - NOT Missing, BUT Opt-In**:

1. **Code Definition**: Fully implemented in `ChannelType` enum with all necessary infrastructure
2. **Onboarding**: Present and complete with `WhatsAppForm` (lines 3325-3505)
3. **Settings/Channels Page**: Present and complete with modal (lines 751-1100)
4. **Configuration**: 
   - Requires explicit opt-in: `"whatsapp"` must be added to `[channels].offered` in `moltis.toml`
   - Default list EXCLUDES WhatsApp (must be explicitly added)
   - Template shows example commented out

5. **JavaScript References**:
   - Onboarding: `channelDisplayLabel()` (line 3477) handles WhatsApp
   - Onboarding channel selector has WhatsApp entry (line 2369)
   - Page-channels has WhatsApp buttons (line 492-499)
   - Both pages conditionally render WhatsApp based on `offered` set

### 6. **Server-Side Channel Data Flow**

**Gateway State** (`crates/gateway/src/state.rs`, lines 288, 326-331):
- Stores `channels_offered: Vec<String>` from config
- Initialized with default if not configured

**Web Template** (`crates/web/src/templates.rs`, lines 401-526):
```rust
// Read from config at page render time
let channels_offered = resolve_channels_offered(cached_channels_offered);

// Build channel descriptors for each offered channel
let channel_descriptors: Vec<ChannelDescriptor> = channels_offered
    .iter()
    .filter_map(|s| s.parse::<ChannelType>().ok())
    .map(|ct| ct.descriptor())
    .collect();
```

**Gon Data Passed to Frontend** (`crates/web/src/templates.rs`, lines 73-74, 475-476):
- `channels_offered: Vec<String>` - list of offered channel type strings
- `channel_descriptors: Vec<ChannelDescriptor>` - metadata for each channel (capabilities, modes, etc.)

Both are injected into the page as gon data and accessed via `getGon("channels_offered")` and `getGon("channel_descriptors")` in JavaScript.

---

## Key Findings

1. **WhatsApp is Implemented**: Not missing—it's a complete, first-class channel with all infrastructure. It requires explicit configuration to enable.
2. **Slack is Intentionally Onboarding-Lite**: Slack is available in Settings but NOT in the onboarding wizard. It can only be added after setup completes.
3. **Default Channel List** (in code): `["telegram", "msteams", "discord", "slack", "matrix", "nostr"]`
4. **Default Onboarding Fallback**: `["telegram", "discord", "slack", "matrix"]` (msteams, nostr, whatsapp excluded)
5. **Opt-in Architecture**: WhatsApp must be explicitly added to `moltis.toml` `[channels].offered` to appear in UI.
6. **Configuration Point**: Edit `moltis.toml`:
   ```toml
   [channels]
   offered = ["telegram", "msteams", "discord", "slack", "matrix", "nostr", "whatsapp"]
   ```

   226→    /// Slack bot accounts, keyed by account ID.

   237→    pub extra: HashMap<String, HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>>,

   239→
   240→impl ChannelsConfig {
   241→    /// All named channel fields as `(channel_type, accounts)` pairs.
   242→    ///
   243→    /// This is the single source of truth for the set of named channel types.
   244→    /// Keep in sync with the struct fields.
   245→    fn named_fields(&self) -> [(&str, &HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>); 6] {
   246→        [
   247→            ("telegram", &self.telegram),
   248→            ("whatsapp", &self.whatsapp),
   249→            ("msteams", &self.msteams),
   250→            ("discord", &self.discord),
   251→            ("slack", &self.slack),
   252→            ("nostr", &self.nostr),
   253→        ]
   254→    }
   255→
   256→    /// Iterate all channel configs (named + extra) as `(channel_type, accounts)` pairs.
   257→    pub fn all_channel_configs(&self) -> Vec<(&str, &HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>)> {
   258→        let mut v: Vec<(&str, &HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>)> =
   259→            self.named_fields().into_iter().collect();
   260→        for (ct, accounts) in &self.extra {
   261→            v.push((ct.as_str(), accounts));
   262→        }
   263→        v
   264→    }
   265→
   266→    /// Extract the `tools` sub-object for a specific channel account.
   267→    ///
   268→    /// Channel accounts are stored as `serde_json::Value`, so we deserialize
   269→    /// just the `tools` key on demand.
   270→    pub fn tool_policy_for_account(
   271→        &self,
   272→        channel_type: &str,
   273→        account_id: &str,
   274→    ) -> Option<ChannelToolPolicyOverride> {
   275→        let accounts = self
   276→            .all_channel_configs()
   277→            .into_iter()
   278→            .find(|(ct, _)| *ct == channel_type)
   279→            .map(|(_, accounts)| accounts)?;
   280→        let account_val = accounts.get(account_id)?;
   281→        let tools_val = account_val.get("tools")?;
   282→        serde_json::from_value::<ChannelToolPolicyOverride>(tools_val.clone()).ok()
   283→    }
   284→}

   294→    ]

Perfect! Now I have the complete flow. Let me create a summary document of my findings:

## Summary: WhatsApp QR Code Pairing Flow Analysis

I've traced the end-to-end flow for the WhatsApp QR code pairing in the onboarding UI. Here's the complete picture:

### The Flow

**Frontend (onboarding-view.js:**
1. User enters account ID and clicks "Start Pairing" → calls `addChannel("whatsapp", id, config)` (line 3403)
2. **CRITICAL:** Event listener is subscribed BEFORE the API call (line 3383):
   ```javascript
   unsubRef.current = onEvent("channel", (p) => {
       if (p.account_id !== id) return;
       if (p.kind === "pairing_qr_code") {
           setQrData(p.qr_data);
           setQrSvg(p.qr_svg || null);  // This is the SVG generated by backend
       }
   });
   ```
3. The UI waits for either `qrData` or `qrSvg` to be set. If neither arrives, it shows "Waiting for QR code..."

**API Call Chain (addChannel):**
- `channel-utils.js` line 172: `sendRpc("channels.add", { type, account_id, config })`
- `gateway/methods/services/channels.rs` line 33: Routes to `ChannelService.add()`
- `gateway/channel.rs` line 252-297: `add()` calls `registry.start_account(channel_type, account_id, config)`

**Backend WhatsApp Plugin (whatsapp/plugin.rs):**
- Line 153: `start_account()` calls `connection::start_connection()`

**WhatsApp Connection (whatsapp/connection.rs):**
- Line 21-155: Spawns a background tokio task with the WhatsApp bot event loop
- The event loop runs asynchronously and **emits events to the event sink**

**Event Handler (whatsapp/handlers.rs):**
- Line 54-142: `handle_event()` processes whatsapp-rust events
- Line 61-77: When `Event::PairingQrCode` arrives:
  ```rust
  Event::PairingQrCode { code, .. } => {
      // Store in local state
      if let Ok(mut qr) = state.latest_qr.write() {
          *qr = Some(code.clone());
      }
      mirror_latest_qr(&accounts, &state.account_id, Some(code.clone()));
      
      // Emit to event sink
      if let Some(ref sink) = state.event_sink {
          sink.emit(ChannelEvent::PairingQrCode {
              channel_type: ChannelType::Whatsapp,
              account_id: state.account_id.clone(),
              qr_data: code,
          }).await;
      }
  }
  ```

**Event Sink Broadcasting (gateway/channel_events/sink.rs):**
- Line 17-55: `emit()` function receives the ChannelEvent
- Line 34-46: **KEY STEP** - For `PairingQrCode` events:
  ```rust
  #[cfg(feature = "whatsapp")]
  if let ChannelEvent::PairingQrCode { ref qr_data, .. } = event {
      if let Ok(code) = qrcode::QrCode::new(qr_data) {
          let svg = code.render::<qrcode::render::svg::Color>()
              .min_dimensions(200, 200)
              .quiet_zone(true)
              .build();
          map.insert("qr_svg".into(), serde_json::Value::String(svg));
      }
  }
  ```
- Line 49-53: Broadcasts via WebSocket with `broadcast(state, "channel", payload, ...)`

**WebSocket Broadcasting (gateway/broadcast.rs):**
- Line 83-159: Sends the event frame to all subscribed WebSocket clients
- Scope guards ensure only authenticated clients receive the event

**WebSocket Frontend (websocket.js):**
- Line 1448: Client subscribes to "channel" events on connect
- Line 1398-1410: `dispatchFrame()` routes events to `eventListeners["channel"]`

**Event Dispatch (events.js):**
- Line 4-13: `onEvent()` registers handlers to `eventListeners[eventName]`
- Events are called with `h(frame.payload || {})`

**Back to Onboarding Form:**
- The listener's payload contains: `{ kind: "pairing_qr_code", channel_type: "whatsapp", account_id: "...", qr_data: "...", qr_svg: "..." }`
- Sets `qrData` and `qrSvg` state, which triggers the UI to display the QR code

### Potential Issues Where QR Code Might Not Appear

1. **Event subscription happens before account is created** (intended behavior but must be reliable):
   - If the event is emitted during `registry.start_account()` before the handler is set up, it could be missed
   - However, line 3383 subscribes BEFORE the API call at line 3403, so this should be safe

2. **Event sink is None** (whatsapp/handlers.rs line 70):
   - If `state.event_sink` is None, the event is silently dropped
   - This happens if the event sink wasn't properly injected during plugin initialization

3. **Broadcast condition** (gateway/broadcast.rs line 154):
   - `drop_if_slow: true` means slow clients are silently skipped (line 50)
   - If the channel is full, the event is dropped without logging

4. **WebSocket not subscribed yet**:
   - If the client hasn't subscribed to "channel" events before the QR code is emitted, the event won't be routed to listeners
   - But onboarding.js ensures the listener is set up before the API call returns

5. **SVG rendering fails** (gateway/channel_events/sink.rs line 35):
   - If `qrcode::QrCode::new(qr_data)` fails, the SVG won't be generated
   - But the frontend has a fallback: it displays `qr_data.substring(0, 200)` if `qrSvgUrl` is null (line 3428)

6. **Missing whatsapp feature flag**:
   - The SVG rendering is gated behind `#[cfg(feature = "whatsapp")]` (line 31)
   - If the whatsapp feature isn't enabled in the build, the QR code SVG won't be generated

### Key File Locations

- **Frontend onboarding form:** `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/clever-oboe/crates/web/src/assets/js/onboarding-view.js` (lines 3325-3475)
- **WhatsApp event handler:** `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/clever-oboe/crates/whatsapp/src/handlers.rs` (lines 54-142)
- **Event sink broadcasting:** `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/clever-oboe/crates/gateway/src/channel_events/sink.rs` (lines 17-55)
- **Connection startup:** `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/clever-oboe/crates/whatsapp/src/connection.rs` (lines 21-155)
- **WebSocket subscription:** `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/clever-oboe/crates/web/src/assets/js/websocket.js` (lines 1432-1453, 1398-1410)

    pub async fn run(&mut self) -> Result<BotHandle> {
        if let Some(receiver) = self.sync_task_receiver.take() {
            let worker_client = Arc::downgrade(&self.client);
            self.client
                .runtime
                .spawn(Box::pin(async move {
                    while let Ok(task) = receiver.recv().await {
                        let Some(worker_client) = worker_client.upgrade() else {

                        };

                        worker_client.process_sync_task(task).await;
                    }
                    info!("Sync worker shutting down.");

}

impl BotHandle {
    /// Abort the bot's run task.
    pub fn abort(&self) {
        self._abort_handle.abort();
    }
}

impl std::future::Future for BotHandle {
    type Output = Result<(), futures::channel::oneshot::Canceled>;

    fn poll(
        mut self: Pin<&mut Self>,
        cx: &mut std::task::Context<'_>,
    ) -> std::task::Poll<Self::Output> {
        Pin::new(&mut self.done_rx).poll(cx)
    }
}

pub struct Bot {
    client: Arc<Client>,
    sync_task_receiver: Option<async_channel::Receiver<crate::sync_task::MajorSyncTask>>,
    event_handler: Option<EventHandlerCallback>,
    pair_code_options: Option<PairCodeOptions>,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for Bot {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("Bot")
            .field("client", &"<Client>")
            .field("sync_task_receiver", &self.sync_task_receiver.is_some())
            .field("event_handler", &self.event_handler.is_some())
            .field("pair_code_options", &self.pair_code_options.is_some())
            .finish()
    }
}

impl Bot {
    pub fn builder() -> BotBuilder<Missing, Missing, Missing, Missing> {
        BotBuilder::new()

impl<B, T, H, R> BotBuilder<B, T, H, R> {
    pub fn on_event<F, Fut>(mut self, handler: F) -> Self
    where
        F: Fn(Event, Arc<Client>) -> Fut + Send + Sync + 'static,
        Fut: Future<Output = ()> + Send + 'static,
    {
        self.event_handler = Some(Arc::new(move |event, client| {
            Box::pin(handler(event, client))
        }));
        self
    }

    /// Register a custom handler for a specific encrypted message type
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `enc_type` - The encrypted message type (e.g., "frskmsg")
    /// * `handler` - The handler implementation for this type
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// The updated BotBuilder
    pub fn with_enc_handler<Eh>(mut self, enc_type: impl Into<String>, handler: Eh) -> Self
    where
        Eh: EncHandler + 'static,
    {
        self.custom_enc_handlers
            .insert(enc_type.into(), Arc::new(handler));
        self
    }

But a simpler approach is to add polling directly in the onboarding form using `sendRpc("channels.status")` and extracting the QR data.

> AGENT

Pushed successfully. Here's what I fixed:

**Root cause**: The WhatsApp QR code was delivered exclusively via WebSocket events. If the event fired before the frontend subscription was fully active, or was dropped due to channel backpressure (`drop_if_slow: true`), the QR code was lost forever — the UI showed "Waiting for QR code..." indefinitely.

**Fix (2 parts):**

1. **`plugin.rs`**: Exposed the `latest_qr` data in `ChannelHealthSnapshot.extra` so the QR code is available via the existing `channels.status` RPC endpoint

2. **`onboarding-view.js` + `page-channels.js`**: Added a polling fallback (every 2s) that fetches QR data from `channels.status` when the WebSocket event hasn't arrived. Polling stops once the QR code is obtained or the modal is closed.

Rebuild and restart the server to try pairing again.

Perfect! Now I have all the information needed. Let me provide a comprehensive analysis:

## E2E Test Infrastructure Overview

I've thoroughly explored the e2e test infrastructure for Moltis. Here's the complete guide for writing WhatsApp QR code pairing flow tests:

### Directory Structure

```
crates/web/ui/e2e/
├── base-test.js          # Shared Playwright fixture with error capture
├── helpers.js            # Shared test utilities
├── mock-oauth-server.js  # Mock OAuth server
├── README.md             # Comprehensive documentation
├── start-gateway*.sh     # Gateway startup scripts for different test scenarios
└── specs/                # Test files (30+ specs total)
    ├── onboarding.spec.js         # Main onboarding flow tests
    ├── channels-nostr.spec.js     # Channel setup tests (pattern reference)
    ├── smoke.spec.js              # Basic app shell tests
    ├── chat-input.spec.js         # Chat interaction tests
    ├── auth.spec.js               # Authentication tests
    └── [26 other test files]
```

### Test Configuration (playwright.config.js)

The test suite uses **multiple isolated Playwright projects** with separate gateway instances:

| Project | Purpose | Server | Port Env Var | Seeded Identity |
|---------|---------|--------|--------------|-----------------|
| `default` | Main tests | Standard | `MOLTIS_E2E_PORT` | Yes (no password) |
| `auth` | Password login tests | Same as default | Same | Yes (password set) |
| `onboarding` | Onboarding flow tests | Special | `MOLTIS_E2E_ONBOARDING_PORT` | **No** (triggers onboarding) |
| `onboarding-auth` | Remote auth simulation | Special | `MOLTIS_E2E_ONBOARDING_AUTH_PORT` | No |
| `onboarding-anthropic` | Anthropic-specific onboarding | Special | `MOLTIS_E2E_ONBOARDING_ANTHROPIC_PORT` | No |

**Key features:**
- **Serial execution** (`workers: 1`) — tests share a single server
- **Automatic port allocation** via `pickFreePort()` to avoid conflicts
- **Free binary detection** — checks `target/debug/moltis` or `target/release/moltis` before `cargo run`
- **Reusable servers** — controlled by `MOLTIS_E2E_REUSE_SERVER=1` env var
- **Environment setup** — `MOLTIS_CONFIG_DIR`, `MOLTIS_DATA_DIR`, `MOLTIS_SERVER__PORT` passed to gateway

### Gateway Startup Scripts

**`start-gateway.sh`** (Default - with completed onboarding):
1. Creates `target/e2e-runtime/{config,data}` (fresh each run)
2. Seeds `IDENTITY.md` and `USER.md` → skips onboarding wizard
3. Detects pre-built binary or uses `cargo +nightly-2025-11-30 run`

**`start-gateway-onboarding.sh`** (Onboarding mode):
1. Same as above BUT does NOT seed identity files
2. App enters onboarding wizard on first load
3. Used for testing onboarding flows, including channel setup

### Shared Test Utilities (helpers.js)

**Core helpers you'll use:**

```javascript
// Navigation & readiness
expectPageContentMounted(page)       // Wait for #pageContent children > 0
navigateAndWait(page, path)          // Goto + content mounted + error check
waitForWsConnected(page, timeoutMs)  // Wait for WebSocket connection (statusDot.connected class)

// Error handling
watchPageErrors(page)                // Collect uncaught page errors into array
  // Usage: const pageErrors = watchPageErrors(page); ... expect(pageErrors).toEqual([]);

// Session management
createSession(page)                  // Click new-session button, wait for key change + URL update
openChatMoreModal(page)              // Open chat "More controls" modal
closeChatMoreModal(page)             // Close it
```

**RPC calling from tests** (from chat-input.spec.js pattern):
```javascript
async function sendRpcFromPage(page, method, params) {
  // Imports helpers.js sendRpc() function and executes RPC
  return await page.evaluate(
    async ({ methodName, methodParams }) => {
      const appScript = document.querySelector('script[type="module"][src*="js/app.js"]');
      const appUrl = new URL(appScript.src, window.location.origin);
      const prefix = appUrl.href.slice(0, appUrl.href.length - "js/app.js".length);
      const helpers = await import(`${prefix}js/helpers.js`);
      return helpers.sendRpc(methodName, methodParams);
    },
    { methodName: method, methodParams: params }
  );
}
```

### Base Test Fixture (base-test.js)

Every test should import from `base-test.js`, not `@playwright/test`:
```javascript
const { test, expect } = require("../base-test");
```

**Features:**
- Automatic error context capture on failure (attaches markdown snapshot)
- Shows URL, title, and visible text for all open pages in failure logs
- Enables faster CI troubleshooting without downloading trace artifacts

### Shared Test Pattern

All specs follow this structure:

```javascript
const { expect, test } = require("../base-test");
const { navigateAndWait, watchPageErrors, waitForWsConnected } = require("../helpers");

test.describe("Feature name", () => {
  test("test name", async ({ page }) => {
    const pageErrors = watchPageErrors(page);  // Always watch errors
    
    // Navigate and wait for ready
    await navigateAndWait(page, "/path");
    await waitForWsConnected(page);
    
    // Perform assertions
    await expect(page.locator("#element")).toBeVisible();
    
    // Assert no errors at end
    expect(pageErrors).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

### Channel-Related Testing (channels-nostr.spec.js Pattern)

**How channels appear in gon data:**

From `crates/web/src/templates.rs` `build_gon_data()`:
```rust
let channels_offered = resolve_channels_offered(cached_channels_offered);
let channel_descriptors: Vec<moltis_channels::ChannelDescriptor> = channels_offered
    .iter()
    .filter_map(|s| s.parse::<moltis_channels::ChannelType>().ok())
    .map(|ct| ct.descriptor())
    .collect();

// Both injected into GonData:
GonData {
    channels_offered,          // Vec<String>, e.g. ["telegram", "whatsapp", "nostr"]
    channel_descriptors,       // Vec<ChannelDescriptor> with capabilities
    // ... other fields
}
```

**Testing channel setup flow:**

From `channels-nostr.spec.js`:
```javascript
test("connect button visible when nostr is offered", async ({ page }) => {
  const pageErrors = watchPageErrors(page);
  await navigateAndWait(page, "/settings/channels");  // Navigate to channels page
  await waitForWsConnected(page);

  // Channel descriptors determine which buttons appear
  const addButton = page.getByRole("button", { name: "Connect Nostr", exact: true });
  await expect(addButton).toBeVisible();
  expect(pageErrors).toEqual([]);
});
```

### WhatsApp QR Code Pairing Pattern (onboarding.spec.js)

This is the exact pattern you need for WhatsApp QR code tests:

**Test structure:**
```javascript
test("whatsapp pairing renders SVG QR from channel event", async ({ page }) => {
  const pageErrors = watchPageErrors(page);
  await page.goto("/onboarding");
  await page.waitForLoadState("networkidle");

  // 1. Reach the channel step in onboarding
  const reachedChannel = await moveToChannelStep(page);
  if (!reachedChannel) {
    test.skip(true, "could not reach channel step in this onboarding flow");
    return;
  }

  // 2. Click WhatsApp channel option
  const whatsappSelectBtn = page.getByRole("button", { name: "WhatsApp", exact: true });
  if (await isVisible(whatsappSelectBtn)) {
    await whatsappSelectBtn.click();
  }

  // 3. Fill account ID input
  const accountInput = page.getByPlaceholder("e.g. my-whatsapp");
  if (!(await isVisible(accountInput))) {
    test.skip(true, "WhatsApp onboarding option is not available in this run");
    return;
  }

  const accountId = "e2e-whatsapp";
  await accountInput.fill(accountId);

  // 4. Mock WebSocket to handle RPC calls (channels.add, channels.status)
  await page.evaluate(async () => {
    const onboardingScript = document.querySelector('script[type="module"][src*="js/onboarding-app.js"]');
    const appUrl = new URL(onboardingScript.src, window.location.origin).href;
    const marker = "js/onboarding-app.js";
    const markerIdx = appUrl.indexOf(marker);
    const prefix = appUrl.slice(0, markerIdx);
    const state = await import(`${prefix}js/state.js`);
    const wsOpen = typeof WebSocket !== "undefined" ? WebSocket.OPEN : 1;
    
    state.setConnected(true);
    state.setWs({
      readyState: wsOpen,
      send(raw) {
        const req = JSON.parse(raw || "{}");
        const resolver = state.pending[req.id];
        if (!resolver) return;
        
        if (req.method === "channels.add") {
          resolver({ ok: true, payload: {} });
        } else if (req.method === "channels.status") {
          resolver({ ok: true, payload: { channels: [] } });
        } else {
          resolver({ ok: false, error: { message: `unexpected rpc: ${req.method}` } });
        }
        delete state.pending[req.id];
      },
    });
  });

  // 5. Trigger pairing flow
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Start Pairing", exact: true }).click();

  // 6. Emit channel event with QR code (CRITICAL PART FOR QR TESTING)
  await page.evaluate(
    async ({ accountIdArg }) => {
      const onboardingScript = document.querySelector('script[type="module"][src*="js/onboarding-app.js"]');
      const appUrl = new URL(onboardingScript.src, window.location.origin).href;
      const marker = "js/onboarding-app.js";
      const markerIdx = appUrl.indexOf(marker);
      const prefix = appUrl.slice(0, markerIdx);
      const events = await import(`${prefix}js/events.js`);
      
      // SVG QR code as string
      const svg = "<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 21 21'><rect width='21' height='21' fill='#fff'/><rect x='2' y='2' width='5' height='5' fill='#000'/></svg>";
      
      // Get channel event listeners and emit pairing_qr_code event
      const listeners = events.eventListeners.channel || [];
      listeners.forEach((handler) => {
        handler({
          kind: "pairing_qr_code",              // Event kind
          channel_type: "whatsapp",              // From ChannelEvent enum
          account_id: accountIdArg,              // Matches filled input
          qr_data: "2@mock_payload",             // Raw QR data string
          qr_svg: svg,                           // SVG rendered as data URI
        });
      });
    },
    { accountIdArg: accountId },
  );

  // 7. Assert QR code rendered
  const qrImage = page.locator('img[alt="WhatsApp pairing QR code"]');
  await expect(qrImage).toBeVisible();
  await expect(qrImage).toHaveAttribute("src", /data:image\/svg\+xml;utf8,/);
  await expect(page.getByText("2@mock_payload")).toHaveCount(0);  // Raw data not visible
  
  expect(pageErrors).toEqual([]);
});
```

### Channel Event System

**Event bus pattern** (from `events.js` import in tests):
- Call `await import("...js/events.js")`
- Access `events.eventListeners.channel` array
- Each listener is a function that receives `ChannelEvent` objects
- Event types from `crates/channels/src/plugin.rs`:

```rust
pub enum ChannelEvent {
  PairingQrCode {
    channel_type: ChannelType,      // "whatsapp"
    account_id: String,              // User input value
    qr_data: String,                 // QR payload ("2@xxx")
    // NOTE: qr_svg added by frontend, NOT in backend enum
  },
  PairingComplete { ... },
  PairingFailed { reason: String },
  // ... other events (InboundMessage, OtpChallenge, etc.)
}
```

**Critical detail:** The test injects `qr_svg` field (not part of Rust enum) — this is frontend-only for testing the SVG rendering.

### Gon Data Injection in Tests

Channels offered at runtime come from `gw.inner.read().await.channels_offered`:
- Must be enabled in the backend config or moltis.toml
- Tests don't manipulate gon data directly; channels appear automatically if configured
- Check if channel is available: `page.getByRole("button", { name: "WhatsApp", exact: true })`
- Skip test gracefully if unavailable

### File Size & Test Naming

- Max 1,500 lines per spec file (use multiple files if needed)
- Test names should be descriptive: `"whatsapp pairing renders SVG QR from channel event"`
- Use `.spec.js` extension for all test files in `specs/`

### Common Selectors & Patterns

```javascript
// From channels-nostr.spec.js
page.getByRole("button", { name: "Connect Nostr", exact: true })  // Channel button
page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Connect Nostr", exact: true }) // Modal heading
page.locator('input[data-field="accountId"]')                      // Field input
page.locator('select[data-field="dmPolicy"]')                      // Select field
page.getByText("How to set up Nostr DMs")                         // Instructions text

// General patterns
page.locator("#pageContent")                                       // Main app content
page.locator("#statusDot")                                         // WS connection indicator
page.locator("#chatInput")                                         // Chat message input
```

# Run specific project
npx playwright test --project=onboarding
```

### Critical Patterns Summary

1. **Always use base-test.js** — provides error context on failure
2. **Always watch page errors** — `const pageErrors = watchPageErrors(page); ... expect(pageErrors).toEqual([]);`
3. **WebSocket mocking** — Import `state.js`, set `state.setWs()` with custom `send()` handler
4. **Event emission** — Import `events.js`, iterate `events.eventListeners.channel`, call handlers
5. **Async script detection** — Find script by `src*="js/..."` attribute, extract prefix, use it for imports
6. **Graceful skip** — Skip tests if optional features unavailable: `test.skip(true, "reason")`
7. **Serial execution** — Tests run one at a time (no parallelism), so ordering matters
8. **Fresh isolated state** — Each spec gets fresh gateway instance (or reused if `MOLTIS_E2E_REUSE_SERVER=1`)

Now I understand. On startup, the gateway loads stored channels from the database and starts them. The user previously added "main" via onboarding — it got persisted to `moltis.db`. On restart, the gateway starts it from the database. When the user hits the onboarding again and clicks "Start Pairing" for "main", it tries to start it again — sled is already locked by the first instance.

The fix: the `add` method in `channel.rs` should check if the account is already running and, if so, return success (or stop and restart). Let me also fix the WhatsApp plugin's `start_account` to handle this gracefully:

The fix is straightforward: if the account is already running, skip re-starting it and return success. This way re-adding from onboarding works:

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_017nuTiVyMWtUTvXpNkCSsfH
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/clever-oboe/crates/whatsapp/src/plugin.rs",
  "old_string": "    async fn start_account(\n        &mut self,\n        account_id: &str,\n        config: serde_json::Value,\n    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {\n        let wa_config: WhatsAppAccountConfig = serde_json::from_value(config)?;\n\n        info!(account_id, \"starting WhatsApp account\");\n\n        connection::start_connection(\n            account_id.to_string(),\n            wa_config,\n            Arc::clone(&self.accounts),\n            self.data_dir.clone(),\n            self.message_log.clone(),\n            self.event_sink.clone(),\n        )\n        .await\n        .map_err(|e| moltis_channels::Error::unavailable(format!(\"whatsapp start: {e}\")))?;\n\n        Ok(())\n    }",
  "new_string": "    async fn start_account(\n        &mut self,\n        account_id: &str,\n        config: serde_json::Value,\n    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {\n        // If the account is already running (e.g. started from stored channels\n        // on boot), skip re-starting to avoid sled lock conflicts.\n        if self.has_account(account_id) {\n            info!(account_id, \"WhatsApp account already running, skipping start\");\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        let wa_config: WhatsAppAccountConfig = serde_json::from_value(config)?;\n\n        info!(account_id, \"starting WhatsApp account\");\n\n        connection::start_connection(\n            account_id.to_string(),\n            wa_config,\n            Arc::clone(&self.accounts),\n            self.data_dir.clone(),\n            self.message_log.clone(),\n            self.event_sink.clone(),\n        )\n        .await\n        .map_err(|e| moltis_channels::Error::unavailable(format!(\"whatsapp start: {e}\")))?;\n\n        Ok(())\n    }"
}

> AGENT

Pushed. Here's what this commit adds:

**Bug fix — duplicate account start:**
- `plugin.rs`: `start_account()` now checks `has_account()` first. If the account is already running (loaded from DB on boot), it returns `Ok(())` instead of trying to open a second sled lock. This fixes the "Resource temporarily unavailable" error you saw.

**E2E test — QR polling fallback:**
- `onboarding.spec.js`: New test `"whatsapp pairing falls back to polling channels.status for QR"` mocks the WebSocket so `channels.add` succeeds but no QR event fires. Instead, `channels.status` returns QR data in the `extra` field. The test verifies the polling picks it up and displays it within 10s.

**Rust test:**
- `plugin.rs`: `has_account_returns_false_when_empty` — verifies the guard predicate.

To fix your immediate issue: kill any lingering moltis process (`pkill moltis` or check `lsof .moltis/whatsapp/whatsapp/main/db`), then restart. The duplicate-start guard will prevent this from happening again.

> AGENT

The e2e test mock returns `{ ok: true, payload: { channels: [...] } }` which is correct — the mock's `resolver()` wraps it. But the test mocks the WebSocket `send()` which calls `resolver({ ok: true, payload: {...} })` directly. The `sendRpc` promise resolves with that object, so `res.payload.channels` is the right path. The mock was correctly shaped, but the *production code* I wrote accessed `res.result` instead of `res.payload`. The test didn't catch it because the mock bypasses the real WebSocket frame parsing, and the test asserted QR visibility based on the mock data flowing through the event system, not through the polling path.

Actually wait — the polling e2e test I wrote DOES test the polling path. Let me check why it would have passed... The mock `send()` handler returns the response directly to the resolver, so `res` = `{ ok: true, payload: { channels: [...] } }`. The polling code does `res.result?.channels` which would be `undefined?.channels` = `undefined`, so `(undefined || []).find(...)` = nothing found. The QR would never be set. The test should have failed!

The test would have caught it IF it were actually run. The e2e tests require a running server and weren't executed yet. Let me fix the code, commit, and push:

> AGENT

Pushed. Added `.skip_history_sync()` to the bot builder — whatsapp-rust 0.5 supports this natively. A bot only needs new inbound messages, so syncing 290+ past conversations and 1.2MB+ of data is unnecessary overhead. The pairing should now complete much faster.

You'll need to delete the existing sled store (`rm -rf .moltis/whatsapp/whatsapp/main`) and re-pair to get the skip-history-sync behavior, since the old pairing already completed with sync enabled.

Now I understand. The self-chat detection in handlers.rs DOES bypass access control for the owner's self-chat messages. But the "Senders" page shows the raw message log entries, which record the access check result. Let me check — is the user sending messages from a *different* phone to their WhatsApp bot number, or are they using self-chat?

Looking at the sender `33650799387@s.whatsapp.net` — this IS the paired number. So these are self-chat messages or messages from another person whose number happens to be... no, it IS the owner's number.

The likely issue: messages from other people coming INTO the bot have a DIFFERENT sender JID, but the owner messaging themselves from another device goes through self-chat. With 12 messages showing "Denied", this means the self-chat detection is failing.

The self-chat detection relies on `get_pn()` and `get_lid()` returning the owner's JIDs. But I think the real issue is simpler: the user is NOT doing self-chat. They're messaging the bot from a different phone or from someone else's WhatsApp. The sender number `33650799387` happens to be the same as the paired account — meaning someone else is sending to them, and the chat_jid is the sender's JID, not the owner's.

Actually wait — no. In WhatsApp DMs, `chat_jid` = the other party. If user A messages bot B, then `chat_jid = A`, `sender_jid = A`. The self-chat check compares `chat_jid` to the owner — which would only match in self-chat (messaging yourself).

So the sender `33650799387` IS the owner, sending from another device to themselves. The `chat_jid` would be `33650799387` which matches the owner. Self-chat detection should work.

But when `is_from_me` is true AND it IS self-chat, then `!is_self_chat` = false, and if it's not a bot echo, we proceed with `is_owner_self_chat = true`. This should work.

The 12 "Denied" messages suggest self-chat detection IS working for some messages (they got processed, not ignored) but access was denied. Wait — if `is_owner_self_chat` is true, access should be `Ok(())`. Unless the messages are NOT from self-chat at all.

  "new_string": "/// Auto-add the owner's phone number to the allowlist so they're always\n/// approved without needing manual configuration or OTP.\nfn auto_approve_owner(\n    accounts: &AccountStateMap,\n    account_id: &str,\n    pn_user: &str,\n    pn_jid: &str,\n) {\n    let mut map = accounts.write().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());\n    let Some(state) = map.get_mut(account_id) else {\n        return;\n    };\n    let already = state\n        .config\n        .allowlist\n        .iter()\n        .any(|entry| entry == pn_user || entry == pn_jid);\n    if !already {\n        info!(\n            account_id,\n            phone = pn_user,\n            \"auto-adding owner phone number to allowlist\"\n        );\n        state.config.allowlist.push(pn_jid.to_string());\n    }\n}\n\nfn should_ignore_inbound_chat(source: &wacore::types::message::MessageSource) -> bool {\n    source.chat.is_status_broadcast() || source.is_incoming_broadcast()\n}"
}

    /// Override the device properties sent to WhatsApp servers.
    /// This allows customizing how your device appears on the linked devices list.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `os_name` - Optional OS name (e.g., "macOS", "Windows", "Linux")
    /// * `version` - Optional app version as AppVersion struct
    /// * `platform_type` - Optional platform type that determines the device name shown
    ///   on the phone's linked devices list (e.g., Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Desktop)
    ///
    /// **Important**: The `platform_type` determines what device name is shown on the phone.
    /// Common values: `Chrome`, `Firefox`, `Safari`, `Edge`, `Desktop`, `Ipad`, etc.
    /// If not set, defaults to `Unknown` which shows as "Unknown device".
    ///
    /// You can pass `None` for any parameter to keep the default value.
    ///
    /// # Example
    /// ```rust,ignore
    /// use waproto::whatsapp::device_props::{self, PlatformType};
    ///
    /// // Show as "Chrome" on linked devices
    /// let bot = Bot::builder()
    ///     .with_backend(backend)
    ///     .with_device_props(
    ///         Some("macOS".to_string()),
    ///         Some(device_props::AppVersion {
    ///             primary: Some(2),
    ///             secondary: Some(0),
    ///             tertiary: Some(0),
    ///             ..Default::default()
    ///         }),
    ///         Some(PlatformType::Chrome),
    ///     )
    ///     .build()
    ///     .await?;
    ///
    /// // Show as "Desktop" on linked devices
    /// let bot = Bot::builder()
    ///     .with_backend(backend)
    ///     .with_device_props(None, None, Some(PlatformType::Desktop))
    ///     .build()
    ///     .await?;
    /// ```
    pub fn with_device_props(
        mut self,
        os_name: Option<String>,
        version: Option<wa::device_props::AppVersion>,
        platform_type: Option<wa::device_props::PlatformType>,
    ) -> Self {
        self.os_info = Some((os_name, version, platform_type));
        self
    }

> AGENT

Pushed. Three fixes:

1. **Auto-approve owner**: On `Event::Connected`, the owner's phone number JID is automatically added to the allowlist so they won't get "Denied" by their own config.

2. **Device name**: Set `.with_device_props(None, None, Some(PlatformType::Desktop))` and `.with_push_name("Moltis")` — the linked device will show as "Desktop" instead of "Unknown device". You'll need to re-pair (delete `.moltis/whatsapp/whatsapp/main` and re-scan QR) for the new device name to take effect.

3. **Button layout**: Added `flex-wrap` to the Connect buttons container so they wrap to multiple rows on narrower viewports.

Now let me address the auto-approve issue. The owner is still showing as "Denied". The `auto_approve_owner` function modifies the in-memory config, but the sender log entries were created BEFORE the Connected event fired (messages arrived during pairing). Let me check if the issue is that `auto_approve_owner` runs but the existing message log entries still show "Denied":

The real issue: `auto_approve_owner` only modifies the runtime config copy inside the `AccountState`. It doesn't update the stored channel in `moltis.db`. And the messages logged as "Denied" before connect will stay that way. But NEW messages after connect should be approved.

However, the user says they still see "Denied" — meaning either:
1. The messages were all sent before `Event::Connected` fired

> AGENT

OK, `current_config` reads from the accounts map. And `auto_approve_owner` writes to the accounts map. So after connect, the config in the map should have the owner's JID in the allowlist. But there's a subtlety: the handler receives `state` (which has its OWN copy of config) and `accounts` (the shared map). The `auto_approve_owner` updates the MAP copy, and `current_config` reads from the MAP. So it should work.

BUT — `auto_approve_owner` takes a write lock on `accounts`. And the handler's `handle_message` reads the config via `current_config(accounts, ...)`. If the Connected event fires AFTER some messages are already queued, the message log would show "Denied" for messages that arrived before auto-approve ran.

The 10 messages the user sees were likely all sent during/right after pairing, before `Event::Connected` fired. After that, new messages should be approved.

   847→/// approved without needing manual configuration or OTP.
   848→fn auto_approve_owner(accounts: &AccountStateMap, account_id: &str, pn_user: &str, pn_jid: &str) {
   849→    let mut map = accounts.write().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());

   851→        return;
   852→    };

   859→        info!(

  "old_string": "/// Auto-add the owner's phone number to the allowlist so they're always\n/// approved without needing manual configuration or OTP.\nfn auto_approve_owner(accounts: &AccountStateMap, account_id: &str, pn_user: &str, pn_jid: &str) {\n    let mut map = accounts.write().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());\n    let Some(state) = map.get_mut(account_id) else {\n        return;\n    };\n    let already = state\n        .config\n        .allowlist\n        .iter()\n        .any(|entry| entry == pn_user || entry == pn_jid);\n    if !already {\n        info!(\n            account_id,\n            phone = pn_user,\n            \"auto-adding owner phone number to allowlist\"\n        );\n        state.config.allowlist.push(pn_jid.to_string());\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Auto-add the owner's phone and LID JIDs to the allowlist so they're\n/// always approved without manual configuration or OTP.\nfn auto_approve_owner_jids(\n    accounts: &AccountStateMap,\n    account_id: &str,\n    own_pn: Option<&Jid>,\n    own_lid: Option<&Jid>,\n) {\n    let mut map = accounts.write().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());\n    let Some(state) = map.get_mut(account_id) else {\n        return;\n    };\n\n    for jid in own_pn.into_iter().chain(own_lid.into_iter()) {\n        let jid_str = jid.to_string();\n        let user = &jid.user;\n        let already = state\n            .config\n            .allowlist\n            .iter()\n            .any(|entry| entry == user || entry == &jid_str);\n        if !already {\n            info!(\n                account_id,\n                jid = %jid_str,\n                \"auto-adding owner JID to allowlist\"\n            );\n            state.config.allowlist.push(jid_str);\n        }\n    }\n}"
}

The polling is working — the WS responses have `qr_data` AND `qr_svg`. The QR SVG is there. The issue is that the polling code sets `qrData` but the SVG isn't being converted to a blob URL for the `<img>` tag.

Looking at the code flow: the polling sets `setQrData()` and `setQrSvg()`, and then the `useEffect` watching `qrSvg` creates a blob URL. But looking at the probe cache — the response uses the cached result which might not be the latest. Actually wait, the responses clearly have `qr_svg` in them.

The real problem: the `channels.add` RPC returned OK (account already running, skip start), so `pairingStarted` is `true`. But the polling `useEffect` has a dependency on `[pairingStarted, qrData]` — when `pairingStarted` becomes true and `qrData` is null, it starts polling. The first poll gets `qr_data` and `qr_svg`, sets them. This should work.

But wait — did you rebuild the JS assets? The dev server serves from disk, so the JS should be the latest. Let me check if maybe the `setQrSvg` call path is broken. Let me look at the onboarding view rendering code — the `qrSvgUrl` is derived from `qrSvg` via a separate `useEffect`. If `qrSvg` is set but the blob URL effect hasn't run yet, `qrSvgUrl` is null, and the fallback shows raw `qrData` as text (which is what you'd see — the base64 text).

Actually, I think the issue is that the `qrSvg` being set via the polling path is an SVG **string** but the blob URL effect expects... let me check if the issue is the SVG XML prefix. The server-rendered SVG starts with `<?xml version="1.0" standalone="yes"?>` which may cause the blob URL creation to fail silently.

I see — the flow is:

1. `addChannel` call fires
2. On success, `setPairingStarted(true)` 
3. The polling `useEffect` starts because `pairingStarted` becomes true
4. First poll hits `channels.status`, gets `qr_data` + `qr_svg`
5. `!qrData` is true (still null), so `setQrData` and `setQrSvg` fire

This should work on paper. But wait — the WS event path (line 3412-3420) also fires `setQrData`/`setQrSvg`. If the WebSocket event fires BEFORE the polling starts, `qrData` would already be set via the WS event. Let me check...

Actually, looking more carefully at the WS logs the user provided: the `channels.status` responses are from the **polling** (request IDs `ui-18`, `ui-19`, etc. — every 2 seconds). This confirms polling IS running and getting data. But the UI still shows "Waiting for QR code...".

The issue is likely that `qrData` got set via the WS `onEvent` callback (line 3414-3416), but the WS event might not include `qr_svg`. Wait — the sink code adds `qr_svg` to the WS event too. Let me check.

Actually, re-reading the summary: "I see no more QR code". This might mean it was working before but stopped. Let me look more carefully at the `!qrData` guard — after the first QR is set, subsequent polls won't update because `!qrData` is false. If the QR code was set once (via WS event) but the SVG wasn't included in that first event, it would be stuck with `qrData` set but `qrSvg` null.

The real bug: the `!qrData` guard prevents QR updates after the first set. The polling should always update if the data changes.

> AGENT

The fix addresses the root cause: **stale closure bug in the polling useEffect**.

In `onboarding-view.js`:
1. The `!qrData` guard prevented QR data updates after the first set — if the WS event set `qrData` without `qr_svg`, the polling couldn't fill in the missing SVG
2. Having `qrData` in the dependency array caused the interval to tear down and recreate on every QR update, creating gaps where polls were missed
3. The "QR cleared = pairing complete" detection relied on the stale `qrData` closure — switched to a ref (`hadQrRef`) that's always current

In `page-channels.js`:
1. Same `!waQrData.value` guard removed — though signals don't have the closure issue, the guard still unnecessarily prevented QR rotation updates

The polling now unconditionally updates QR data whenever it's present in the response, and the interval runs steadily without being torn down on state changes.
